TopicRetriever#invalid_host? does check that the URL host equals embeddable_host, so arbitrary-host SSRF is limited to the configured embeddable_host, but topic retrieval throttling is a per-URL redis key ('retrieved:#{@embed_url}') with 60s expiry, so unlimited distinct paths on that host can trigger server-side fetches and topic creation as the embed_by_username user. The throttle bypass also exists via staff user_id. This is a genuine security/abuse concern introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, any request that passes `ensure_embeddable` (based solely on `request.referer` host) will enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, without validating `params[:embed_url]` itself or applying rate limiting at the controller level. The job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can result in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` doing a server-side `open(url)` and creating/updating a topic/post as `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`). The redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed by the full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can bypass it by varying URLs/paths, enabling unbounded fetches/auto-topic creation (at least for URLs on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, since `invalid_host?` blocks other hosts).
